formalObservation.Composition:
The composition is strongly horizontal and contains several distinct figure-like forms distributed across a shared ground.

Three dominant structures:

- large cylindrical/rounded figure on the left
- smaller low horizontal figure near the centre
- large rectangular/rounded figure on the right

Additional small forms appear between and beneath the principal figures.

A broad irregular horizontal ground runs through the lower portion.
formalObservation.Primary Forms:
Left figure:

- large cylindrical body/head
- two circular eye-like forms
- wide mouth
- repeated triangular tooth-like marks
- projecting appendage to left
- projecting hand/limb-like form toward right
- two narrow lower supports

Central figure:

- horizontally oriented low form
- rounded head
- eye-like marking
- open mouth
- triangular tooth-like marks
- small projecting appendages
- short lower support structure

Right figure:

- large vertically oriented rounded/rectangular figure
- two eye-like forms
- open mouth
- triangular tooth-like marks
- prominent lower facial/body projection
- lateral appendage
- narrow lower supports
formalObservation.Secondary Forms:
- small central rounded form
- horizontal projecting structure
- small circular/oval forms
- irregular ground elements
formalObservation.Structural Forms:
- Horizontal ground band
- Vertical supports
- Cylindrical body structures
- Rectilinear upper contours
- Rounded lower forms
- Connecting horizontal lines
formalObservation.Repeated Forms:
- Circular eyes
- Triangular tooth marks
- Narrow vertical supports
- Horizontal ground elements
- Parallel hatching
formalObservation.Mark-Making:
Strong horizontal and vertical hatching system:

- dense vertical hatching
- horizontal hatching
- broad contour strokes
- darker filled areas
- repeated short directional marks
- lighter loose construction lines

Hatching frequently extends beyond immediate contours into the surrounding ground.
formalObservation.Spatial Strategy:
Horizontal / Relational / Grounded

Figures are arranged along a common horizontal axis. The lower ground structure provides a visual base connecting multiple elements.
formalObservation.Figure–Ground Relationship: Figures remain strongly legible against paper while hatching and ground forms create connections between them.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Strong horizontal composition.
- Several large figure-like forms occupy a common ground.
- Each major figure has a distinct structural configuration.
- Repeated circular eyes and triangular mouth marks create formal continuity.
- Cylindrical, rectangular and organic contours coexist.
- Ground lines connect otherwise independent forms.
- Scale differences establish hierarchy between major figures.
